Zoe (People Ops): FYI Mark filed for a divorce QLE. He needs to remove ex-spouse from coverage and wants to know about COBRA options for the ex, plus any FSA/commuter/HR implications. Timeline? Docs?
Mark T: Yes  separation date 2026-09-20, final decree pending. Spouse currently on plan. I need to remove them ASAP and confirm whether they can elect COBRA and for how long. Also curious if my HSA contributions are affected and whether I need to change beneficiary on life insurance.
Jen - Benefits: Sorry to hear that. Divorce or legal separation is a QLE. We need proof (filing notice or court docs) within 30 days to process removal midyear. Once removed, the ex-spouse is typically eligible for COBRA continuation from the carrier for up to 36 months (depends on state/carrier). We will send COBRA election packet to the ex's address on file unless you provide alternative contact via secure intake.
Mark T: What about the ex's access to dependent FSA? Do they keep coverage like dental and vision?
Jen - Benefits: COBRA covers the same benefits they had while enrolled (medical, dental, vision) subject to carrier COBRA rules. Dependent-care FSA is not COBRA-eligible, but health-care FSA may be (partial rules apply). If you had a family HCFSA and the spouse was a dependent, they may elect continuation for the remaining plan year, but claims are generally limited to expenses incurred during the coverage period. We can provide COBRA packet specifics once we remove them.
COBRABot: Automated: COBRA election window is 60 days from the date the COBRA notice is mailed. Coverage continuation dates and premiums will be in carrier notice. Employer must notify COBRA administrator within 30 days of the QLE; employee-provided documentation helps speed processing.
Noelle (Payroll): Payroll note: removing a dependent will change pre-tax elections. If COBRA is elected, premiums will be paid by the ex directly, not through payroll deductions. Your HSA eligibility: if your plan coverage changes from family to self-only, it may affect HSA contribution limits; update contribution elections via self-service and notify payroll before the next pay period. Also, review life insurance beneficiary forms in Workday if you want to change them.
Legal Intake: If you provide a separation agreement or filing notice with sensitive details, redact financial amounts and SSNs before upload. Send documents via secure HR portal. If the divorce is contested, provide the best available legal filing; we can provisionally process removals with filed proof and update once decree is finalized.
Mark T: I don't want the COBRA packet mailed to our shared address. How can I ensure it's sent to ex directly?
Jen - Benefits: We can request COBRA admin to mail to the ex's personal address if you provide contact details or the ex requests it directly to the admin. To protect privacy, submit the alternate mailing request through secure intake or have your ex call the COBRA number on the benefits site. We'll not post addresses in slack.
Zoe (People Ops): I'll add a 20-day follow-up to ensure docs are uploaded. Mark, please upload the filing notice to https://hr.redwood.com/upload (category: QLE - Divorce). Jen will confirm removal and trigger COBRA notification to admin.
Mark T: Uploading now. Thanks everyone.
Jen - Benefits: Received. Processing removal and will confirm COBRA packet initiation by tomorrow EOD. :thumbsup:
